column4:

column4:
The national open government partnerships include 1) government entities, 2) academia, and 3) business associations and civil society. One of the 4 pillars of its first Open Administration National Action Plan (URL: https://ogp.eportugal.gov.pt/monitorizacao) is precisely open data. OGP Portugal aims to guarantee concrete commitments from governments to promote transparency, encourage public participation, fight corruption, and use new technologies to strengthen participatory democracy - https://ogp.eportugal.gov.pt/inicio. 
In December of 2022, in accordance with the pillars of the second Open Administration National Action Plan 2022 (URL: https://ogp.eportugal.gov.pt/ii-panaa), AMA launched the Mosaico platform (URL: https://mosaico.gov.pt/) which promotes universal access to information between the state and the citizen.
Besides OGP, other examples are: 
1) Arquivo.pt, which promotes an annual contest for innovative works carried out based on open data (preserved by Arquivo.pt). Arquivo.pt is developed by the Scientific Computing Unit of FCT - Foundation for Science and Technology - https://sobre.arquivo.pt/pt/conheca-os-vencedores-do-premio-arquivo-pt-2022/. 
2) The Urban Co-Creation Data Lab is a project that aims to provide support on decision making at the city level on high-quality services for citizens. The project is a collaboration between the Portuguese government (AMA) and NOVA IMS University. The project supports new planning and management approaches altogether with new tools to evaluate the impact and predict various services demand (URL: https://www.urbandatalab.pt/). 
3) The DSPA represents the Data Science sector and promotes data science in Portugal and internationally. The association also promotes regulation, ethics, and security in the field of data science. It shares experiences, innovations, case-studies, and success stories and promotes innovation and entrepreneurship of Portuguese companies (URL: https://dspa.pt/)

column2:
Have any public bodies in your country developed any systematic way of gathering reuse cases?

For Explanation:
* If yes, please provide a brief explanation of the process: How does the gathering happen?
column4:
[Response to reviewer] 
The ongoing project entitled "Open Data - Impact Assessment Model Definition" (URL: https://www.base.gov.pt/Base4/pt/detalhe/?type=contratos&id=9601046) has implemented systematic methods for collecting (re)use cases, incorporating best practices (while also accounting for the cautionary lessons) from reports such as "Rethinking the Impact of Open Data," "The Economic Impact of Open Data," and "The Use Case Observatory Volume I" available on data.europa.eu.
The systematic methods for gathering eligible entities for building use cases about the impact they create when (re)using open data are the following prioritization rules:
a) having ongoing or scheduled data platforms, explicit data policies, data quality control procedures, and/or a general knowledge of its platform users
b) the data platform is in the form of a website, data portal, or web application
c) entities can be classified as private, public (government) or academic institutions
d) entities can maintain regular and effective communication with the Administrative Modernization Agency, I.P. (AMA)
e) entities can underpin if their operational influence is in at least one of the following sectors: social, governmental, environmental or economic
f) entities can be classified into at least one of the following positions of the open data value chain: data reuser, data portal, data intermediary
Upon their acceptance of the collaboration, they were provided with an impact assessment questionnaire.

column2:
Are there any public bodies in your country that have developed a systematic ways of classifying the gathered reuse cases?

For Explanation:
* If yes, please provide a brief explanation of the process: According to which categories are reuse cases classified (e.g. by policy field)?
column7:
The study from AMA, "Projeto Impacto dos Dados Abertos. Casos de Estudo", categorizes the information of the use cases in different topic areas. 
The reuse cases and their impacts are assessed and classified by data providers and reusers under four possible areas or dimensions: governmental, economic, social, and environmental. The project is implementing surveys to the entities to assess different metrics related to the knowledge and evidence of the impacts of the reuse cases in each of the four dimensions. This allows the measure of the impact of the open data in each dimension and to perform a global analysis, from which the cases can be classified considering their impacts. This was already applied in a set of reuse cases, and future plans include applying it to a larger set. [Please check the file attached to this survey Relatório Casos de Estudo.pdf]
The metrics that are being produced in the context of this project were inspired on “Rethinking the impact of open data” (Ooijen et al., 2023), “The Use Case Observatory” (Carsaniga, Dogger e Regeczi, 2022), “European DATA Market Study 2021–2023” (European Commission, 2023a), “Creating Value through Open Data” (Capgemini Consulting et al., 2015) e “The economic impact of open data” (Huyer e Knippenberg, 2020).

column7:
1- Publishing data on the dematerialization of medical paper prescriptions by electronic means exemplifies how open data has a substantial impact on the efficiency and effectiveness of a government in delivering public services by reducing administrative burdens, eliminating paper-based processes, enhancing accuracy, facilitating faster access to prescriptions, and enabling seamless coordination among healthcare providers, ultimately resulting in improved healthcare delivery and patient care outcomes (URL: https://transparencia.sns.gov.pt/explore/dataset/desmaterializacao-eletronica-da-receita/table/?sort=periodo).
2- The use of open data on illegal parking (URL: https://urbandatalab.pt/index.php/component/sppagebuilder/?view=page&id=118pen) allows for the identification of patterns and prediction of parking in the city of Lisbon, thus improving surveillance efficiency. 
3- The Primary Health Care Identity Card allows for the proper management and efficiency in the use of health resources (URL: https://www.spms.min-saude.pt/2020/07/bi-csp-bilhete-de-identidade-dos-cuidados-de-saude-primarios/)

column7:
Mais Transparência portal (URL: https://transparencia.gov.pt/pt/) is a digital information platform on various management topics and public resources under the responsibility of AMA - Agency for Administrative Modernization. The information is permanently updated with data available on the national open data portal under the responsibility of the entities.
Mais Transparência Portal allows citizens to access information provided by the Government in a more accessible way, reinforcing their relationship of trust with the Public Administration. The Mais Transparencia Portal , a barometer of the NextGenerationEU fund application at the national and municipal levels, allowing citizens to have access to information through a data visualization tool (URL: https://transparencia.gov.pt/pt/fundos-europeus/prr/barometro/ complemented with straightforward channels for downloading the source open data (URL: https://transparencia.gov.pt/pt/fundos-europeus/prr/barometro/ and technical documentation URL: https://transparencia.gov.pt/pt/fundos-europeus/prr/dimensao/resiliencia/). It also allows evaluating how Portugal compares in the NextGenerationEU fund application to other member states, e.g., URL: https://www.portugal.gov.pt/pt/gc23/comunicacao/noticia?i=portugal-e-dos-paises-mais-avancados-na-execucao-do-prr.
Also, the data on public contracts and procurement provided at base.gov (URL: https://www.base.gov.pt/base4) has been used in academia as a source to study topics related to accountability and transparency in the public sector. Some examples are the following: "Public sector corruption and accountability in cost deviation and overruns of public projects" by  Catalão et al. (2023) (URL: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11115-022-00616-x); "The entanglement of time and cost deviations in public projects" by Catalao et al. (2023)  (URL: https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1111/apce.12364); "Essays on the Socioeconomic Impacts of Digital Government - Chapter 5", by Martins J. (2024) (URL: https://repositorium.sdum.uminho.pt/handle/1822/88833?mode=full)
Futhermore, The Complementary tool to the Electronic national official journal (https://incm-tst.outsystemsenterprise.com/INOV_DRE/Home) offers open access to legal information and fosters a deeper comprehension of laws and regulations, thereby ensuring transparency in decision-making processes and facilitating accountability by empowering citizens to hold public administrations responsible through enhanced accessibility to legal content; 
Finally, the Open data and statistics regarding criminality indicators https://partilha.justica.gov.pt/Transparencia/Cadernos-Tematicos/Criminalidade is a tool that allows research journalists to delve deeper into, for example, corruption crimes, allowing long-term assessments of the state of anti-corruption efforts with detailed accounts of the number of investigations, convictions and sentences and, thus, substanciate trends in levels of criminality, severity of penalties, rates of case dismissals, duration of investigation and appropriateness of investigative resource allocation.

column7:
The Ministry of Health in Portugal is responsible for the open data initiative known as the "Transparency Portal". The primary objective of this initiative is to ensure full access and transparency to a wide range of data concerning the operations and transactions of the National Health System (SNS). This involves information from different organizations involved in providing healthcare nationwide. This portal has a significant impact on health:Access to detailed health data allows for better monitoring of health outcomes, identification of trends, and early detection of issues, enabling timely interventions and also, Policymakers and health administrators can use this data to make informed decisions regarding healthcare policies, resource allocation, and management of healthcare services.
Other examples:
1- The "Resposta Sazonal em Saúde" (Seasonal Health Response) is a platform with interactive dashboards of the daily updates on the progression, accessibility, and use of healthcare services by citizens, namely primary Healthcare, hospital healthcare, and emergency healthcare. It provides timely information to the populace and healthcare sector stakeholders, facilitating their effective preparedness for response https://www.sns.gov.pt/plano-de-contingencia-sazonal/
2- The Daily Evolution of Emergency Calls seeks to inform the public on health initiatives, resource allocation, and the development of preventive measures.URL: https://transparencia.sns.gov.pt/explore/dataset/acionamentos-de-meios-de-emergencia-medica/table/?sort=periodo
In particular, it allows to monitor the response times relative to the number of daily emergency events and determine the nation-wide average response time as well as allow nation-wide media outlets to create awareness on the public to sub-optimal response times https://expresso.pt/sociedade/2022-10-23-INEM-demorou-uma-hora-ou-mais-a-acionar-meios-em-mais-de-mil-chamadas-d36ee608 
3 - The "Centro de Saúde Fora de Horas" (After-hours Healthcare Centers, URL: https://www.arslvt.min-saude.pt/centros-de-saude-fora-de-horas/#14) is a data visualization map of healthcare centers with extended working hours. Its primary goal is to reduce the demand for hospital emergency services among patients who, while experiencing an acute illness, do not require such specialized care. This tool has been featured in national-level media outlets, e.g., https://www.publico.pt/2022/11/23/sociedade/noticia/portal-sns-passa-informacao-centros-saude-abertos-ate-tarde-2028846
Link for more information: https://transparencia.sns.gov.pt/page/ajuda/

In fact, Directorate-General for Education and Science Statistics (DGEEC) provide data that can be freely used, reused and redistributed by anyone, without restrictions of copyright, patents or other control mechanisms, and which subject, at most, to the requirement to cite the source. According to this question, open data is available for all data that does not require authorisation to be processed, and this is the case for all DGEEC statistical data available on the website.
In our website, you can access to our open data for example concerning:

https://www.dgeec.medu.pt/art/6499db7d9eff36f307f07bdb/65293837121f641a986cc618/653b96736ac1e15eea50c5db/6566f1631a5e26972f636ebe#artigo-661e1fb548f22fa765197a7a  

Then, you can also access to 7 datasets: https://dados.gov.pt/pt/organizations/direcao-geral-de-estatisticas-da-educacao-e-ciencia-dgeec/?datasets_page=7#organization-datasets.
1) Reuse cases: https://dados.gov.pt/pt/organizations/direcao-geral-de-estatisticas-da-educacao-e-ciencia-dgeec/?datasets_page=7#organization-reuses
2) Examples of Open Dataset used by the reuse case: 
- https://empregocientificoedocente.dgeec.mec.pt/ ; 
- https://dados.gov.pt/pt/reu; 
3) Description: For example InfoCursos Portal (https://infocursos.medu.pt/), is a tool that presents data and statistics on the Higher Professional Technician (TeSP), 1st cycle Bachelor's, Integrated Master's and 2nd cycle Master's programmes offered by Portuguese higher education institutions. The ‘Course statistics’ tab shows information for all courses that had students enrolled in the 1st year for the first time, according to the data reported to the DGEEC by higher education establishments through the RAIDES survey. No statistics are provided for military or police courses. The ‘Course data’ tab shows the information contained in the Guide to Entrance Exams, issued by the Directorate-General for Higher Education, for 1st cycle Bachelor's and Integrated Master's programmes.

This is a project included in a broader initiative that try to use the different educations databases and give some added value for the differentes users. In this area, it includes also Info escolas – focus in non-higher education information and where we can found several indicators as (mainly at a school level and compared with student similar students’ background):
• Students who completed the 1st cycle in 4 years (%)
• Students from poor background who completed the 1st cycle in 4 years
• Students who completed upper sec in 3 years (%) and succeeded in the national exams
• Students who completed the VET programmes in 3 years
• Comparison between students’ internal and national assessment scores
• Progression between 9th and 12th grades scores

Returning to the InfoCursos portal (http://infocursos.pt), it was developed in 2015 (as part of a bigger initiative that included also infoescolas portal) provides data and statistics on the mains Higher Education programs (Technical Vocational Courses (TeSP), 1st cycle degrees, Integrated Masters and 2nd cycle Masters), taught at Portuguese higher education institutions. Is also part of the measures to fight failure and dropout in higher education.

Infocursos is a “need to improve” result, for allowing:
1. To increase public information about the educational system
2. To improve the technical quality of the indicators available to the educational community
3. To transform results and demographic indicators in a more qualitative information, that can contribute to a better knowledge of the education system
But, more important was the Infocursos portal allows students, together with their families, to make a supported decision when choosing the higher education course they wish to follow. 

In the same perspective, we can refer InfoEscolas Portal (https://infoescolas.medu.pt/) as a “need to improve” result, for allowing:
1. To increase public information about the educational system
2. To improve the technical quality of the indicators available to the educational community
3. To give back to schools statistical data useful for self-evaluation processes
4. To transform results and demographic indicators in a more qualitative information, that can contribute to a better knowledge of the education system.
